1:2.translation: All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

words.explanation: The starting noun of the sentence. It is definite and marfūʿ, ending in ḍammah (-u).
Preposition لِ ('to/for') + اللَّهِ. The phrase 'belongs to Allah' acts as the khabar (predicate): 'the praise → (belongs) to Allah'.

words.role: naʿt / badal of Allah, and muḍāf
words.explanation: Describes اللَّهِ, so it follows it in the genitive. It is also the muḍāf (first noun) of the iḍāfah رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ.
The second noun of the iḍāfah ('of the worlds'), always genitive. The sound masculine plural marks genitive with -īna.

options: Because it is the subject of the sentence
Because it describes اللَّهِ (which is genitive) and is also a muḍāf
Because it comes after a verb
questions.explanation: It is a description (naʿt/badal) of اللَّهِ, so it matches it in the genitive; it is simultaneously the muḍāf of رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ.

questions.q: Which word is the mubtadaʾ (starting subject)?
questions.explanation: الْحَمْدُ is the definite noun that begins the sentence and is marfūʿ — the mubtadaʾ.

questions.q: Which word is the muḍāf ilayh in رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ?
questions.explanation: الْعَالَمِينَ is the second, genitive noun of the iḍāfah.

1:5.translation: It is You we worship, and You we ask for help.

words.explanation: A detached object pronoun ('You') placed BEFORE the verb for emphasis and exclusivity: 'You ALONE we worship'. Fronting the object restricts the meaning.
Present-tense verb (root ع ب د). The subject 'we' is contained in the prefix نَ-. Marfūʿ because it is an unaffected present verb.
Form X verb from root ع و ن ('to seek help'). The fronted إِيَّاكَ before it again means 'You alone we ask for help'.

questions.q: Why does إِيَّاكَ come BEFORE the verb نَعْبُدُ?
options: Fronting the object gives exclusivity: 'You ALONE we worship'
It is required by all Arabic verbs
questions.explanation: Placing the object before the verb restricts the action to that object — 'You alone we worship'.

words.explanation: Imperative 'Say' (root ق و ل). Its subject 'you' is contained within it.
'He' — the starting subject of the sentence inside the speech of 'Say'.
Identifies the subject: 'He is Allah'. Marfūʿ, ending in ḍammah.
'One' — the predicate giving the key information. Indefinite, so it ends in tanwīn (-un).

questions.q: What case is أَحَدٌ, and how can you tell?
options: Nominative — it ends in tanwīn ḍammah (-un)
questions.explanation: أَحَدٌ ends in -un (tanwīn ḍammah), marking it marfūʿ (nominative) as the predicate.
